body.statement: Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and let \(\mathcal O_G\) be its observed moments for an arbitrary view graph \(G\). A permutation \(\pi\) is a source-to-sink path in \(\mathcal D_G\) if and only if \(\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\). For every such path, each \(Q_{\pi,j}\) has a positive-definite completion obtained as a coordinate principal block of a full residual covariance, and independently assembling these completed blocks yields a component-aligned Gaussian completion with coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\).
body.justification: This closes the only load-bearing model-specific composition boundary between observable recursive tests and globally valid arbitrary-pairing completions.
body.gap: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, treats fully paired recursive identification, while GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion, Theorem 7, characterizes chordal completion patterns. Neither composes an arbitrary view-graph root path with coordinatewise positive-definite noise completion on maintained LiMVAM inputs.
body.consumer: Analysts with only selected paired view cohorts obtain an exact population certificate that every emitted coefficient tuple belongs to a full component-aligned mechanism.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(L^{0,(a)}=I_p-B^{0,(a)}\), and let \(\Sigma_{\rm full}\) denote the
covariance of the full vector \((X^{(a)}:a\in M)\), including the conceptually
present nonedge blocks.  By \(\texttt{ass:shared-topological-order}\), every
\(L^{0,(a)}\) is unit triangular after the common permutation \(\pi_0\), hence
is invertible.  By \(\texttt{ass:component-aligned-disturbances}\), the full
disturbance covariance \(\Omega\) satisfies
\[
 \Omega[(a,i),(b,j)]={\bf1}\{i=j\}\,\Gamma_i[a,b].
\]
After grouping indices by \(i\), this matrix is
\(\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i)\).  Every block is positive definite
by \(\texttt{ass:disturbance-positive-definiteness}\), so \(\Omega\succ0\).
The structural equations in
\(\texttt{ass:linear-structural-equations}\) now give
\[
 \Sigma_{\rm full}
 =\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})^{-1}
   \Omega
   \operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L^{0,(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
 \succ0.
\]
Consequently every \(\Sigma^{aa}\) and every principal matrix
\(\Sigma^{aa}[A,A]\) is positive definite.  The inverses in
\(\texttt{def:modified-cholesky}\),
\(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\), and
\(\texttt{def:q-root-score}\) therefore exist.  Moreover, each within-view
Schur complement \(C_A^{aa}\) is positive definite, so
\(C_A^{aa}[r,r]>0\).  This justifies every division below.

We first prove the path criterion.  Orthogonal projection onto the span of
\(X_A^{(a)}\), followed by projection onto the residual of \(X_r^{(a)}\), is
orthogonal projection onto the span of \(X_{A\cup\{r\}}^{(a)}\): both sides
are orthogonal to that span, and an orthogonal projection is unique because
its Gram matrix is positive definite.  Hence, for
\(t\in U_A\setminus\{r\}\),
\[
 Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}
 =Z_{A,t}^{(b)}-
   \frac{C_A^{bb}[t,r]}{C_A^{bb}[r,r]}Z_{A,r}^{(b)}.
\]
Taking covariance with \(Z_{A,r}^{(a)}\) and using symmetry of
\(C_A^{bb}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P\!\left(
 Z_{A,r}^{(a)},Z_{A\cup\{r\},t}^{(b)}\right)
 =C_A^{ab}[r,t]-C_A^{ab}[r,r]
   \{C_A^{bb}[r,r]\}^{-1}C_A^{bb}[r,t]
 =q^{ab}(A,r,t).                                      \tag{1}
\]
This also proves from \(\texttt{def:projected-residual-state}\) that the
state after removing a set is a function of that set and the fixed covariance
blocks, rather than of the path used to reach it.

Fix a permutation whose next label after \(A\) is \(r\), and let
\(W=U_A\setminus\{r\}\) in the order supplied by the suffix.  Sequential
within-view regression of the variables in \(W\) gives an invertible unit
triangular matrix \(K^{(b)}\) such that the final innovation vector is
\[
 e_W^{(b)}=K^{(b)}Z_{A\cup\{r\},W}^{(b)},
 \qquad e_r^{(a)}=Z_{A,r}^{(a)}.
\]
Equation (1) therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_r^{(a)},e_W^{(b)})
 =\bigl(q^{ab}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)(K^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}.       \tag{2}
\]
Since \(K^{(b)}\) is invertible, the left side of (2) is zero if and only if
all its displayed \(q^{ab}\)-scores are zero.  Reversing \(a,b\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_W^{(a)},e_r^{(b)})
 =K^{(a)}\bigl(q^{ba}(A,r,t):t\in W\bigr)^{\mathsf T},        \tag{3}
\]
so both orientations in \(\texttt{def:removed-set-compatibility-dag}\) are
necessary and sufficient for the row and column involving \(r\) to have no
off-diagonal entries.  Applying (2)--(3) successively along the permutation,
with the one-variable suffix as the base case, proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
 \text{ for every }\{a,b\}\in E.                            \tag{4}
\]
The same normal equations show that \(R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal for every
view: an earlier innovation is orthogonal to the span on which every later
variable is regressed.

It remains to verify, rather than assume, the completion part of
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\).  For an arbitrary \(\pi\), let
\[
 L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad S_\pi=L_\pi\Sigma_{\rm full}L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit triangular in order \(\pi\), so it is invertible,
and the already proved \(\Sigma_{\rm full}\succ0\) gives \(S_\pi\succ0\).
For \(j\in V\), let \(H_{\pi,j}\) be the principal submatrix of \(S_\pi\)
on the indices \(\{(a,j):a\in M\}\).  Principal submatrices of a positive
definite matrix are positive definite, because for nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^m\)
its zero extension \(\widetilde u\) satisfies
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}H_{\pi,j}u
 =\widetilde u^{\mathsf T}S_\pi\widetilde u>0.
\]
For a diagonal view block or an observed edge, the corresponding block of
\(S_\pi\) is exactly
\(L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T}=R_\pi^{ab}\).
Thus \(H_{\pi,j}\) agrees with every specified entry of \(Q_{\pi,j}\) and is
a positive-definite completion.  This conclusion holds for every candidate
order and every arbitrary view graph on a maintained-model input.  Combining
it with (4) and \(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) proves
\[
 \pi\text{ is a source-to-sink path in }\mathcal D_G
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G).    \tag{5}
\]

Finally suppose (equivalently by (5)) that these conditions hold.  For each
\(j\), choose the just-constructed completion
\(\Gamma_j^\pi=H_{\pi,j}\), and take mutually independent centered Gaussian
vectors \((\eta_j^{(a)}:a\in M)\) with covariances \(\Gamma_j^\pi\).  Put
\(\eta^{(a)}=(\eta_j^{(a)}:j\in V)\) and define
\[
 \widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\eta^{(a)}.
\]
Then the coefficient matrices are exactly \(B_\pi^{(a)}\), share order
\(\pi\), and satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_i^{(a)},\eta_j^{(b)})=0
 \quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad \operatorname{Cov}((\eta_j^{(a)})_{a\in M})
 =\Gamma_j^\pi\succ0.
\]
Thus the assembled law satisfies all five member properties in
\(\texttt{def:component-aligned-limvam-class}\); Gaussianity makes the
independently assembled coordinate stacks a joint centered Gaussian vector.
On diagonal blocks and edges, (4) and the within-view diagonality give
\(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta^{(a)},\eta^{(b)})=R_\pi^{ab}\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)},\widetilde X^{(b)})
 =(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{ab}(L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma^{ab}.
\]
The constructed completion therefore has the observed law
\(\mathcal O_G\) and coefficient tuple \(T_\pi\), as claimed.
